extracted.intended_audience: literate readers, writers, critics, and citizens interested in poetry, literature, and the cultural health of American democracy
extracted.subtask_description: An essayistic treatment combining literary-criticism guidance (especially about poetry) with cultural and political argument about the role of literature and nature in American democracy. Includes memoiric practical notes on starting newspapers and authorial practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic melody and universal accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Longfellow is eminent in the style and forms of poetical expression that mark the present age (an idiosyncrasy, almost a sickness, of verbal melody) ... poet of melody, courtesy, deference ... universal poet of women and young people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuate poetry that brings what is dearest to the general human heart and taste; favor melodic, courteous, deferential verse that soothes and heals rather than shocks. Such work strikes a 'splendid average' and appeals broadly rather than courting exception or revolt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation over revolutionary excess
rubrics_metrics.description: He is not revolutionary, brings nothing offensive or new, does not deal hard blows. On the contrary, his songs soothe and heal, or if they excite, it is a healthy and agreeable excitement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid extreme, offensive, or deliberately shocking material when the aim is broad human sympathy; gentle anger or critique (even 'at second hand') is preferable in many poetic contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intuitive selection and judgment of poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: I doubt if there ever was before such a fine intuitive judge and selecter of poems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trust an intuitive, sympathetic sense when choosing or translating poems; this instinct is a legitimate critical faculty and may yield choices (including translations) superior to literal vernacular originals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations as potentially superior renderings
rubrics_metrics.description: His translations of many German and Scandinavian pieces are said to be better than the vernaculars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A translation judged by vitality and spirit can surpass literal originals; assess translations on poetic effect and living quality rather than strict literal fidelity alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry's meaning need not be fully definable
rubrics_metrics.description: Common teachers or critics are always asking 'What does it mean?' ... who shall fathom and define those meanings?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept that poetry often conveys meanings that elude precise intellectual definition; critics should not insist on fully explicating every poetic effect. This is not a license for 'wildness and frantic escapades' but a recognition of legitimate mystery and feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggestiveness and 'what is not gathered' as poetic virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: At its best, poetic lore is like what may be heard of conversation in the dusk, from speakers far or hid, of which we get only a few broken murmurs. What is not gather'd is far more—perhaps the main thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value poems that suggest rather than state, that leave fragments and peripheral intimations for the reader to assemble; the unsaid or implied can be the chief power of a passage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sensuous nature-symbols and imagination in poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: The play of Imagination, with the sensuous objects of Nature for symbols and Faith—with Love and Pride as the unseen impetus and moving-power of all, make up the curious chess-game of a poem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct poems by letting imagination work through sensuous natural images as symbolic carriers of faith, love, and pride; see the poem as a strategic interplay ('chess-game') of these forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceptual strategy: take poetic passages 'at free removes'
rubrics_metrics.description: Grandest poetic passages are only to be taken at free removes, as we sometimes look for stars at night, not by gazing directly toward them, but off one side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appreciate (and read) major poetic passages indirectly—attend to their atmosphere and resonance rather than fixating on direct, literal interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader contribution to meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: I only seek to put you in rapport. Your own brain, heart, evolution, must not only understand the matter, but largely supply it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A poem expects active participation: the reader's experience, history, and sensibility supply critical parts of the poem's effect and meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ultimate judgment by Nature and life, not by technical rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The last deciding tests applicable to a book are entirely outside of technical and grammatical ones, and that any truly first-class production has little or nothing to do with the rules and calibres of ordinary critics? ... the ocean and the daylight, the mountain and the forest, putting their spirit in a judgment on our books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess literary work by its correspondence with lived experience and natural truth rather than solely by formal, grammatical, or encyclopedic technicalities; authenticity and vitality matter most.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve spontaneity and 'outdoor' flavor in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Hardly even the seasons group'd together, or anything corrected--so afraid of dropping what smack of outdoors or sun or starlight might cling to the lines, I dared not try to meddle with or smooth them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assembling memoiric or nature-inflected pieces, avoid over-editing that removes the immediate outdoor quality and spontaneous quality which give the material its character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical requirements for starting a newspaper
rubrics_metrics.description: I went to New York, bought a press and types, hired some little help, but did most of the work myself, including the press-work. Everything seem'd turning out well... I bought a good horse, and every week went all round the country serving my papers, devoting one day and night to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Founding a paper entails practical commitments: machinery (press and type), some hired help but often hands-on labor, distribution logistics, regular rounds to serve subscribers—personal investment and physical work are essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democracy needs regular contact with Nature
rubrics_metrics.description: American Democracy, in its myriad personalities... must either be fibred, vitalized, by regular contact with out-door light and air and growths, farm-scenes, animals, fields, trees, birds, sun-warmth and free skies, or it will certainly dwindle and pale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civic and social health depend on sustained exposure to natural life; cultivate public and private practices that connect people to outdoors as a civic requirement, not merely an aesthetic choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: National literature must be native, original, and pervasive
rubrics_metrics.description: Democracy can never prove itself beyond cavil, until it founds and luxuriantly grows its own forms of art, poems, schools, theology, displacing all that exists, or that has been produced anywhere in the past, under opposite influences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A democratic national identity requires an indigenous literature that originates new forms and pervades institutions (schools, theology) so that it supplants inherited feudal or ecclesiastical cultural holdovers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for high-grade 'literatuses' to shape public life
rubrics_metrics.description: Our fundamental want to-day in the United States... is of a class, and the clear idea of a class, of native authors, literatuses, far different, far higher in grade than any yet known, sacerdotal, modern, fit to cope with our occasions, lands, permeating the whole mass of American mentality, taste, belief...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate and recognize a small number of exceptionally influential writers/thinkers whose work radiates teachers, schools, manners, and helps construct the moral substratum of the republic—literati with near-sacerdotal cultural influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature as primary instrument for social and religious reform
rubrics_metrics.description: View'd... the problem of humanity all over the civilized world is social and religious, and is to be finally met and treated by literature. The priest departs, the divine literatus comes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize literary invention and moral imagination as the decisive means to address social and religious crises rather than relying solely on political, legal, or clerical remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imaginative literature (poetry) central to national identity
rubrics_metrics.description: What I say in these Vistas has its main bearing on imaginative literature, especially poetry, the stock of all... something equivalent to creation is, for our age and lands, imperatively demanded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place imaginative literature at the center of cultural formation—poetry and allied forms are the primary vehicles for forming national character and unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature must penetrate hearts and create perennial sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless it goes deeper, gets at least as firm and as warm a hold in men's hearts, emotions and belief, as, in their days, feudalism or ecclesiasticism, and inaugurates its own perennial sources, welling from the centre forever, its strength will be defective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for works that root themselves emotionally and spiritually among the populace so that literature becomes a durable, internal source of belief and identity rather than a transient intellectual trend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material prosperity is insufficient without moral conscience
rubrics_metrics.description: I would alarm and caution even the political and business reader, and to the utmost extent, against the prevailing delusion that the establishment of free political institutions, and plentiful intellectual smartness, with general good order, physical plenty, industry, &c., do, of themselves, determine and yield to our experiment of democracy the fruitage of success... The element of the moral conscience... seems to me either entirely lacking, or seriously enfeebled or ungrown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate national success not merely by material or institutional metrics (prosperity, suffrage, order) but by the cultivation of moral conscience and genuine belief—these are decisive for lasting democratic health.
